ES
Bark · Polaris Pro · UK & Ireland

Lifecycle analysis and proposal, from signup to trial conversion

Both current flows, piece by piece. A single lifecycle across three routes, with the event logic that fires it. And how I would measure whether it works in revenue, not in opens.

NAMEMario Calvo
ROLESenior CRM Manager
DELIVERABLECase study and live demo

00 · Thesis

Messages go out by date. They should go out by what the Pro does.

Both flows are built on the day of the cycle: the Pro gets the third message because three days have passed, not because they did or failed to do something. That is where the duplicate pieces come from, the ones that contradict each other, and the claims about their visibility the product has not yet delivered.

The proposal swaps the calendar for a state machine. The Pro moves through observable milestones, and time only serves to rescue when a milestone does not arrive.

TodayProposed
The calendar decides the send→A Pro event decides it
Two isolated flows→One lifecycle, three routes
They are told they are already visible→They are shown what actually happened
Ends at the charge→Continues through the subscription

Launch priority: orchestrate the first enquiry within minutes; verify the Pro's real state before making any claim; and close the trial with a transparent value recap, measured against a persistent holdout.

The two current flows

Flow A

Signup → trial start

Seven sends in ten days to Pros who sign up and do not start the trial. In six of the seven I find something the Pro can notice.

D0 Welcome
D1 Identical to D10
D2 Raw preheader · rewrites the profile without permission
D2 297 searches · unsegmented
D5 Contradicts D2
D8 A summary of four zeros
D10 D1 again · closes on zero
Calendar-triggered · no exit condition
Calendar-firstThe send depends on the date rather than the Pro's state, so it goes out even when their real blocker is something else.
RepetitionD1 and D10 are the same email word for word. Only the subject and headline change, nine days apart.
ContradictionD2 ticks «✓ photo added». D5 lists that same photo as outstanding, in red. The rule abort if strong profile never suppressed the email.
SuppressionThere is one suppression rule across the whole programme, and here it does not end up applying. Most of the other findings follow from that.
Flow B

Onboarding during the 7-day trial

It is better built than A: three welcome variants, genuinely segmented. Where I see the problem is the moment that decides the subscription, which it reaches late.

T0 3 variants · segmented
+24h Profile updated
+1d No app
+1d Unanswered enquiry, by email
T6 Single notice before the charge
T7 Three competing asks
Segmented at entry · no reaction to behaviour
WorksThe three welcome variants, and using real marketplace data as proof. The mechanism looks right to me; what I would change is when it fires and on what condition.
LatencyThe unanswered-enquiry alert arrives by email, a day later. To my mind it is the moment of the trial that decides the most revenue.
Pre-chargeOne notice, 24 h before an automatic charge, with no data on what the Pro achieved that week.
AfterI find nothing after day 10 or after the trial ends: CRM stops where revenue starts.
FLOW A

Signup → nurture up to the trial

Piece-by-piece audit: 7 sends, 27 observations and the original screenshots.

day 0 · Email

D0 · Welcome

1 / 7

Welcome to Bark Marketplace

Email
Would improve
Fires on signup, not on eligibility

The brief fires the flow on signup, but does not confirm what determines whether a Pro can appear in searches. I would keep an immediate acknowledgement at signup and gate the rest of onboarding on the real eligibility or visibility state that Product confirms — call it profile_min_complete provisionally, pending the final event name.

day 1 · Email + push

D1 · Start your free trial

2 / 7

Email + push. 'Get up to 3 enquiries free'

Breaks
The subject line promises what is not inside

Subject: 'Free Trial unlocked – get clients for free! ✅'. Preheader: 'You now have free access to marketplace features for 7 days'. Both say the trial is ALREADY active. Inside, the CTA is 'Start a Free Trial Now': it is not active, it has to be activated. My question is what that does to the credibility of the next subject line they get.

It is the same email as D10

Body identical word for word, same creative ('GET 3 MORE FREE ENQUIRIES'), same 'What's included' module. Only the subject and headline change. It sends on day 1 and repeats on day 10 without adding a single new data point, even though by then we know a great deal more about that Pro.

Would improve
It repeats the ask without adding anything

My first reading was that asking for the trial on day 1 is premature. That is wrong: the trial is offered at signup, on Plan & pricing, before card details (CONFIRMED in the Helpcentre). Asking on day 1 is not a CRM error, it is the product's front door.

What is a problem is that this email repeats the same ask with nothing new. If they saw it at signup and did not take it, there is a reason — no reviews on the profile, doubts about price, doubts about demand in their area — and this email addresses none of them. And since the trial is once per account only, the ask only gets one chance to land: better that it arrives once the doubt has been answered, rather than repeating the same offer.

Push and email say the same thing

Two channels, one message, the same hour. The push should carry urgency the email cannot; right now it is a duplicate.

No category or city for the Pro

'Get up to 3 enquiries free' is generic and creates no urgency. With data we already have: '47 people searched for a cleaner in Leeds this week'. The same message goes from abstract promise to concrete, checkable demand — and it is the same data D2 already uses.

day 2 · Email

D2 · Profile updated

3 / 7

'Your profile has been updated, take a look'

Breaks
Preheader leaking raw code

The preview text the Pro sees in the inbox is: 'Customers can now find and contact you. <div style="font-size:1px; display:none!important...'. The hidden div is printing as visible text. It belongs as the first element inside <body>, never in the subject field — and in Iterable the trick is not even needed, the template has its own preheader field.

It rewrites the profile without asking

The copy is explicit: 'we've used information from your website to update your Bark profile', and it lists the photo, description and services it changed. For a sole trader the profile is their shopfront, and here it is edited without them asking. The email also closes with 'you only have a limited time before your ranking is decreased': they are asked to validate a change they did not request, with a penalty if they do not.

It contradicts D5 three days later

Here it ticks '✓ profile photo added' and '✓ description updated'. In D5 those same two items appear in red as outstanding, and the rule abort if strong profile never suppressed the email. Conclusion: what Bark auto-fills does not count towards profile strength. There is no single source of truth for profile state.

Would improve
Publish it as a draft to approve

Same work, published as a draft: 'here is what we found on your site, shall we apply it?'. One click. You get the same complete profile, with consent and without the risk of publishing wrong data, and an interaction from the Pro is logged along the way.

Question
Is it too early?

It lands on day 2, before the 24h demand proof. Fixing the profile is far more persuasive once the Pro has seen that people are searching for what they do. Test the order: demand first, profile fix after.

day 2 · Email

D2 · 24h · demand proof

4 / 7

'297 searches for your service in the last 24h'

Breaks
The strongest data point, and unsegmented

The search count is the strongest argument in the flow. In a niche category or a rural postcode that number is low or zero, and then the same piece works against you. I would branch on demand density by category × geography, with a different message when volume is low.

Would improve
The subject line wastes its best data

The number sits in the body and the subject is generic. I would move it up into the subject: 'Mario, your last 24h on Bark' o '297 people searched for your service yesterday'. It is the only email in the flow whose subject can carry data of the Pro's own.

Works
I would turn this mechanism into a rule

Demand for a category in an area is verifiable and does not depend on the Pro's state: it works even when they have nothing of their own to show yet. I would make it a principle of the flow — market argument by default, and their own numbers only when they exist and are not zero. What I would change is the segmentation, not the idea.

day 5 · Email

D5 · Competition / GIF

5 / 7

Abort if the user has a strong profile

Email
Breaks
It asks for what D2 said it had done

'Upload a profile picture' and 'write a description' appear in red, and they are exactly the two items D2 ticked as done three days earlier. Either day 2 said something that was not accurate, or the system does not recognise its own changes. From the Pro's side the effect is the same.

Would improve
Profile strength as an on/off switch

It suppresses a single email. It should be a continuous score driving the next best action, dynamic content and suppression across the whole programme.

The commercial CTA, hidden in the checklist

The fourth item under 'improve your profile' is 'start your 7-day trial'. The commercial ask is presented as advice. You can do that once; after that the checklist stops reading as help. I would take it out of the checklist and ask outright.

An impossible item: 3★ with zero reviews

'Get an average review score above 3 stars' sent to a newly registered Pro with zero reviews. It is not hard: it is impossible by definition, and the only fix offered is importing them from another platform. An item the Pro cannot complete does not belong on an activation checklist.

Works
The only suppression on the board

It is the right direction: not badgering a Pro who already did what was asked.

day 8 · Email

D8 · Your first week

6 / 7

'1383 searches. What visibility do you have?'

Breaks
It sends with four zeros

The real email shows: 1383 searches for your service · 0 average list ranking · 0 times you have appeared in search · 0 profile views. The piece shows at once that there is demand and that the Pro has received none of it. I understand the intent — use real data — but with the counters at zero the email that should motivate ends up documenting the opposite.

It does not square with what we said in D2

On day 2 we told them 'you now appear in customer search results'. On day 8 we tell them they have appeared 0 times. Only three readings fit: that D2 was not true, that it was true and is not being measured, or that appearing depends on more than the profile. From the outside I cannot tell which, and all three point to the same place: nothing stops a state being claimed without an event to back it.

Would improve
It swaps the argument that works for one they do not have

On day 2 the flow uses the argument that holds: how many people searched for their service. That is market data — verifiable and independent of their state. This email switches to their counters — ranking, appearances, views — which by this point are usually at zero. The weekly recap fits where it is: it is a week. What I would change is what gets shown when their numbers do not back it up.

With the counters at zero, what is still true

If all their counters are 0, the table tells them nothing they do not know. I would replace it with demand in their category and area — which is still true — plus the reason it is not reaching them, once Product confirms what that is. Their own numbers return to the email the moment one of them stops being zero.

day 10 · Email

D10 · Final trial push

7 / 7

'You have 3 free enquiries waiting'

Breaks
It is D1 again, nine days later

Body identical word for word to day 1, same creative, same 'What's included' module. Only the subject and headline change. It is the last touch before the Pro leaves CRM, and it is spent repeating a message that already did not work once.

It closes on a zero

The demand module shows 12,806 searches in their category and a 0 beside it. The market figure is the one that works; theirs, placed next to it, cancels it out. I would keep only the one that leads to an action.

Would improve
It should be a diagnosis, not a third sales push

By day 10 we know they have appeared 0 times. The email could tell them why and what to do: what the profile is missing, how much demand there is in their radius, what specific change unblocks it. That is how the last touch becomes the most useful rather than the most repeated.

And close the door properly

One single ask, without the four-bullet module. Social proof from their own category and area. And an exit promise: 'we will stop writing to you about the trial; we will only get in touch when there is real demand near you'. It is a promise we can keep, and the expectation — to be tested — is that it lowers the unsubscribe rate on the flow's last touch.

FLOW B

Free trial

Piece-by-piece audit: 6 sends, 23 observations and the original screenshots.

day 0 · Email + push · 3 variants

Trial start · 3 variants

1 / 6

Profile in the search list / not listed / no app

Breaks
It contradicts itself inside the same email

The header says 'You've already received customer enquiries'. The final block says 'You're not appearing in customer searches. Customers can't find you because your profile is incomplete'. If they are not appearing in searches, it does not hold that they have received enquiries. Both claims sit in the same piece, one scroll apart.

What matters most to them sits at the end

In the not-visible profile variant, the red block —you are not appearing in searches because your profile is incomplete— is what decides whether the trial is any use to them, and it sits below everything else. I would move it up to the headline and into the subject line: today the subject celebrates the trial, and the reason it will not work for them is four screens of scrolling away.

Would improve
All three describe the system, not the Pro

Visible / not visible / no app is Bark's view. The Pro's view is missing: is there demand in my category this week? I would add demand density as a fourth dimension.

The creative sells what they have already bought

The headline congratulates them —'Congrats, you've started a Plan free trial'— but the image underneath says 'GET MORE CUSTOMER VISIBILITY', which is acquisition language. At that point the Pro has already activated it: there is nothing left to sell them, there is something to confirm. I would swap the hero for the new state — what they can do today that they could not yesterday — rather than repeating the promise that got them here.

Two different events in one piece

The trigger is starting the trial, but the headline is about enquiries received. They are two facts that do not happen at the same time: one is trial_started and the other is enquiry_received. I would split them — the welcome when the trial starts, and the enquiry when it arrives, with its own channel and its own urgency.

The variants are exclusive; the conditions are not

A Pro can have an incomplete profile y not have the app installed at the same time, and only gets one of the two versions. I would treat it as one piece with conditional blocks rather than three emails: the blocks stack according to what they are missing, without forcing a choice.

The push does not say what is missing

The notification tags along without being specific. It could name the exact gap: 'you are missing photos to appear in photographer searches in Leeds'. One data point, one action.

Works
The best-resolved segmentation

Segmenting on the user's real state is the right direction, and it is the only place in the programme that does it. The rest should get here.

+24h · Email

+24h · Profile updated

2 / 6

'We added more information from your website'

Breaks
It notifies a change instead of proposing it

It tells them Bark has changed their photo, their description and their services — the same mechanic as D2 in the signup flow, and the same observation applies here. I would frame it as a proposal the Pro approves: 'here is what we found on your site, shall we apply it?'. You reach the same complete profile, with consent, and an interaction from them is logged along the way.

Would improve
It sends without checking whether D2 already went out

It is the same email as D2, and nothing checks whether it already went out. I would condition it on it not having been sent in the signup flow — a suppression on the event, not on the flow, because a Pro who signs up and then starts the trial goes through both. In the medium term I would consolidate it into a single profile-progress trigger, with the flow as context rather than the owner of the message.

+1d · Email

+1d · No app

3 / 6

'Win jobs faster with the Bark app'

Email
Would improve
The app already does what CRM is doing by hand

The 'Win more enquiries' module says the Bark Assistant analyses the profile and tells them exactly what to improve. If that capability already exists inside the product, D5's static checklist is doing by hand something Bark already does dynamically. I would draw the next action from that same engine, rather than maintaining two lists that can disagree.

The QR opens the piece and does not work on mobile

The first thing it offers is a QR code — 'Scan here to get the app' — inside the header image. If the Pro opens the email on their phone they cannot scan their own screen, and the button that does work sits at the end, after four modules. I would put a direct store link at the top and keep the QR for people opening it on desktop.

Question
+1 day from what?

The material places it at +1 day, but does not say what it counts from. If it is one day after the trial starts, it is a reasonable time-based rescue and I have no objection: it goes to people without the app, with room not to overload them. If it counts from the previous send, the moment shifts every time a piece upstream is suppressed, and frequency stops being something you can reason about globally. It is one of the first things I would ask before touching anything.

+1d · Email

+1d · Unanswered enquiry

4 / 6

'Customers are waiting for a reply'

Breaks
The moment that decides most, by email and late

An unanswered enquiry is a job that can be lost. I would take this to push and SMS within minutes rather than an email the next day: response speed is what the product promises.

It sends the alert, not the enquiry

'Customers are waiting for a reply' makes the Pro log in to find out who, what and when. I would send the enquiry itself: customer name, job, area, how long ago and a reply button. That way it stops being a reminder and becomes the product working. And one per enquiry, not a daily digest.

day 6 · Email

T6 · Your trial ends tomorrow

5 / 6

'…and your Starter Plan begins'

Breaks
A notice with nothing to justify the charge

In a seven-day trial I do not think there is room for three notices: that would be badgering them about something they already know. What this one is missing is not repetition, it is content. It arrives without a single data point on what they achieved and without cancellation in plain sight — the two things that separate a notice from a surprise charge. I would keep one single notice before the charge — date, amount and how to cancel — and move the value recap to an earlier send.

Would improve
The value recap, earlier and not here

Contacts received, jobs, activity that week: without it the money is asked for against a promise; with it, against something they have already seen. Where to put it is the tricky part. Inside this notice it works if the numbers are good; if they are bad, it hands them the reason to cancel exactly when there is no time left to fix anything. I would put it around day 4 or 5: with room for them to act if the result is poor, and as an early warning to us about which Pros are going to cancel.

day 7 · Email

Trial ended · cancelled beforehand

6 / 6

'Your free trial is no longer active'

Email
Breaks
Raw code over the logo

As it appears in this material, the email leaks what looks like a preheader div into the visible body, and the same shows in D1, D2, D8 and D10. It could be a render fault in production, or it could be an artefact of how the screenshots were put together for the exercise: from the outside I cannot tell which. It is one of the first things I would check — if it happens on the real send, a render-QA step is missing between build and send.

The subject and the body do not say the same thing

The subject says 'Your free trial is no longer active'. The body opens with 'Your free trial will end tomorrow'. And the consequences are in the past tense: 'you have been de-ranked', 'you can no longer respond'. Either it has ended or it ends tomorrow, but not both at once.

Three asks competing with each other

It announces the consequences (we have de-ranked you, you can no longer reply), asks for feedback and asks you to pay again. The three asks compete, and the last two get in each other's way: someone who has just left is unlikely to do both.

Would improve
Feedback belongs in the cancellation flow

Asking for the reason inside this email competes with the ask to come back. I would put it where the Pro is cancelling — in product, at the moment of the decision, when it is fresh and when it can actually branch the treatment — and keep a follow-up email a few days later only for those who did not give it there.

It is missing what they did get out of it

My first version of this note proposed 'since it ended: 0', and it does not fit: this is a confirmation email, there has been no time for anything to happen. What does make sense is a block with what they got out of durante the trial — searches they appeared in, enquiries received, replies sent — when the numbers support it. It is their own data, and it is more of an argument than telling them they have been de-ranked.

No offer, no win-back

Someone who has just decided it is not worth it is offered the price they rejected. Without a new reason to come back — a returning rate, a specific enquiry waiting for them — the piece works more as a notification than a win-back.

One lifecycle, three routes

Today, what goes out is decided by the day of the cycle. In the proposal it is decided by where the Pro sits in the milestone chain. The three routes share attributes, suppression and channel priority, and a Pro is only ever in one.

Route 1

Can try it and has not started

trial_eligible AND NOT trial_started
Goal: reduce uncertainty

They saw the trial offer at signup and did not take it. Repeating it unchanged adds nothing; what is needed is an answer to the doubt that stopped them.

· An explicit explanation of the trial: what it includes, when it charges, how to cancel
· Demand by category and area, where the data exists and is representative
· Profile readiness personalises the treatment; it does not block the trial from starting
· Close on inactivity, not on day 10
Route 2

Trial active

trial_started = true
Goal: speed up the chain

Profile ready → impressions → enquiry → reply. Each message pushes the link that Pro is missing, not the next one on the calendar.

· Profile next action: one single thing at a time
· The enquiry within minutes, with the context inside the piece
· A diagnosis when there are no impressions, with the reason and the fix
· A value recap before the charge, with their own numbers
Route 3

Subscriber

subscription_active
Goal: consolidate and recover

It does not exist today. It is where month two renewal is decided, and where failed payments sit unrecovered.

· A monthly value cycle with real data
· Dunning for failed payments, starting by confirming volume and causes
· Cancellation by reason, with a different route per reason

A note on trial_eligible, which lives in the rules rather than in the routes. It is not a segment: on a new signup it is almost always true, and the only reason that applies to someone who has just signed up is their category not offering a trial — that variant changes the ask inside Route 1, it does not create a route. Where the flag does matter is later, so a trial that has already been spent is never offered again. Confirmed

The proposed flow

Three routes. A Pro is only ever in one. Each route reads left to right, and above every step is what fires it. Click any piece to see the mockup, its entry and exit conditions, and what it suppresses while it is active. Every one of those conditions is an event or an attribute that has to exist: checking which ones already do is the first task in the role.

Pro event — sends the moment it happens Time — only if the event never arrived, and cancelled if it does Route exit
Route 1

Can try it and has not started

They saw the trial offer at signup and did not take it.

trial_eligible AND NOT trial_started

If their category offers no trial, it is the same route with a different ask: direct plan fit instead of activating the trial. That variant is flagged, not built.

Time +24 h without starting the trial

✓ Starts the trial Moves to Route 2. Any pending time-based message is cancelled.
✕ Three attempts without starting The route closes: we stop writing about the trial. We only get in touch if real demand appears nearby.
Route 2

Trial active

Has full access and a card already on file.

trial_started = true
8 steps
Enters trial_started
Time +12 h without the app installed

Time +72 h with impressions and no enquiry

Subscriber

The card has been charged; the goal is no longer conversion.

subscription_active

The milestone chain and the states that watch it

Each state answers one question: what is stopping this Pro from reaching the next milestone. And it declares its entry, its exit, what it suppresses and which KPI it moves.

H1
Signup
pro_signed_up
H2
Trial started
trial_started
H3
Profile ready
profile_ready
H4
First impression
marketplace_impression
H5
First enquiry
enquiry_received
H6
First reply
enquiry_replied
H7
First charge
subscription_charged

The rule that changes the system: an event in the chain cancels any time-based message chasing that same milestone. That is where most of the current repetition disappears.

The 31 events and attributes this needs

Every entry and exit condition in the flow rests on one of these. The certainty column is what separates a proposal from a plan: 12 are already used by the current flow, 2 are confirmed in the documentation, and 17 I need without knowing whether they exist. That last group is the instrumentation audit, and it is why that is the first task in the role.

One flow, two pipelines, priority driven by events

A message goes out for one of two reasons: the Pro has done something, or has not done it in time.

Pipeline 1

Event-driven

HIGH PRIORITY · SECONDS

Product emits the event, the Pro's state is recalculated and, if it passes suppression, frequency and consent, it goes out on the channel the action calls for: push if it is immediate, email if it needs context, SMS only as a consented fallback. Content is resolved at send time, not pre-composed.

Pipeline 2

Time-driven

LOW PRIORITY · RESCUE ONLY · CANCELLABLE

Every milestone in the chain has a window; if the milestone does not arrive, a rescue goes out. The specific windows sit on each arrow of the proposed flow, and they all share one rule: the moment the real event happens, the pending rescue is cancelled.

Priority between journeys

Today there is one suppression rule across the whole programme. Without this layer, an incoming enquiry competes with the onboarding messages themselves.

P
Level
What belongs here
1
Security and transactional
Never suppressed. It is not marketing.
Verification, account changes, legal notices
2
Urgent enquiry
Interrupts onboarding, education and commercial. Exits on reply.
Enquiry received without a reply
3
Payment and subscription
Above anything educational. No upsell while a payment is outstanding.
Failed payment, trial ending, cancellation intent
4
Profile ready for the marketplace
One action at a time, the highest-impact one.
Profile component blocking relevance
5
Value proof and commercial
Only with evidence of value behind it.
Recap, plan fit, trial activation
6
Education and discovery
The first thing sacrificed when there is competition.
Tips, features, best practice

The 7 execution rules

It is the contract between CRM and Product. Without it, the state machine stays a diagram.

ID
Rule
How it is implemented
R1
Time only fires if the state has not changed Hypothesis
`after 24h AND state unchanged`. Never «day 3» as a reason in itself.
R2
An enquiry pauses everything else; replying resumes it Hypothesis
`enquiry_received` pauses priority 4 and below. `enquiry_replied` cancels the escalation — including the pending SMS — and re-evaluates the state. It is the case shown live in the demo.
R3
Push first; SMS only as a fallback and with consent Hypothesis
`push_delivered AND NOT enquiry_opened after X` → SMS. Never simultaneous by default. Never SMS for profile education.
R4
Deduplication on `enquiry_id` Hypothesis
Two enquiries do not create two escalation threads for the same one.
R5
A global cap per channel and per Pro Hypothesis
Weekly for email, daily for push. Transactional and urgent do not count towards the cap.
R6
Local hours and quiet hours Hypothesis
Push and SMS within the market's working hours, unless the action is actionable at that time.
R7
No fresh snapshot, no send Hypothesis
If the demand or performance data is incomplete or stale, the message does not go out. Silence beats a false zero.

When it is time to ask about the profile, which of the six

Two moments need it: before the trial, when the profile cannot compete yet, and when the Pro appears in searches but nobody picks them. In both, the rule is to ask for the first thing missing from this list, and only that one, until its exit condition is met.

Order

Stops being asked when
1

reviews_count = 0

reviews_count > 0

photos_count >= 3
3

Define services and a price range
pricing_status = complete
4

service_area_invalid OR service_area_missing
Fix the service area
service_area_valid
5

credentials_status = missing

credentials_status = complete

about_length < minimum
Write the business description
about_complete

Why not `profile_score < 70`. An aggregate score does not tell a Pro with no reviews apart from one with no pricing. Those are two different blockers, with two different actions and two different resolution times. And a threshold of 70 would be a made-up number: there is nothing behind it. Inference

And the order is a proposal, not a finding. It would need agreeing with Product — who already have the analysis: the Bark Assistant reads the profile and says what to improve. The sensible thing is to lean on that engine.

Measurement: retained revenue, not opens

NORTH STAR
Incremental D60 retained subscription revenue per eligible Pro

It joins monetisation and retention in one number. It stops us celebrating a conversion that cancels before the second charge, which is exactly the risk when the subscription activates on its own.

If Finance has margin by plan, use contribution instead of gross revenue. Inference

THE FULL FUNNEL
Trial started → activation → value realised → first charge → retained subscriber

Paid conversion is automatic unless the Pro cancels, so trial-to-paid alone mixes inertia, product and CRM. What genuinely informs is how many Pros reach value during the trial.

Secondary metrics

The ones that explain the main metric

Eligible signup → trial startedEligible Pros only.
Trial → retained after the first charge
First renewalIf the value was real, it survives the second charge.
Time to first replyThe first value the Pro genuinely sees.
Reply rate on the first enquiry
Chargebacks, spam complaints and opt-outsThe guardrail: none of this may get worse while conversion rises.

Vanity metrics. Opens, clicks, deliveries, SMS cost — They tell you why a metric is not moving. They are never the result.

How I will know it works

01 Random assignment before the first message
Every eligible Pro is randomly assigned to the new flow or the current one before receiving anything. Assigning at send time compares people who were already different.
02 A group without the new flow, from day 1
The permanent holdout. It is the only way to know whether the programme adds anything or just reaches Pros who would have converted anyway.
03 The winning metric, fixed before launch
Retained subscription within the agreed window. With limits that must not get worse: chargebacks, complaints and enquiry quality.

«If trial-to-paid goes up, how do you know it was the CRM?»
By comparing the Pros who received the new flow against the holdout, on the metric fixed up front. If the difference survives the first renewal and the limits do not get worse, it was the CRM.

First what costs credibility, then what adds conversion, then optimisation. Foundation holds whatever blocks everything else if it is missing.

Items marked 2 WEEKS are what I would launch in the first two weeks. What I would not build yet: incentives as a blanket layer, founder offers, predictive scoring or twenty journeys — until a diagnosed friction and the data justify them.
